mission: R04c lands: the wound mechanics. Torin lifts the Codex without flinching and holds it steady. The fragment's records name what the Scar actually is — a Force wound sustained and expanded by anchored Force-sensitives, the anchor system as the specific mechanism by which Gavran converted twelve living people into structural rebar. The wound's mechanics resolve from 'damage' to 'engineered architecture held against collapse by human cost.' Torin's rationalisation crystallises into a coherent argument. Ben catches his own head nodding before he stops it. In the corridor afterward, Sera's hand on Ben's arm, back to the door: 'I have heard that argument before. From a man I followed into a war.'
why_now: The Codex's framework is now on the table. With the technique named at R04b and the wound's mechanism specified here, the chain that links Veraine's procedure to Veranthos is legible in outline for the first time. Sera's warning in the corridor lands because Ben has just understood — in his body — the scale of what Torin's reading is trying to justify.
conflict: Torin's reading of the Codex is intellectually beautiful. If the Weave is imposed, the technique is correction rather than violation. The argument is seductive in proportion to how well it fits the evidence — and the evidence, just revealed by R04c, is worse than Ben had let himself understand. Ben's susceptibility is the reader's warning, not his speech.
turning_point: Ben catches the motion of his own head nodding to Torin's last sentence. He stops it. Sera sees him catch it, and pulls him aside.
opening_hook: Torin holds the Codex fragment and doesn't flinch. Everyone else did
closing_hook: Sera, very quietly to Ben: 'I have heard that argument before. From a man I followed into a war.' She doesn't say Gavran's name. She doesn't need to
emotional_trajectory: Absorbing the wound's mechanism -> intellectual engagement with Torin's reading -> seductive logic -> Sera's cold water

stakes.personal: Ben nearly seduced by Torin's interpretation — a warning about his own susceptibility, sharpened by the fact that he has just understood what the wound actually costs
stakes.interpersonal: Sera trusting Ben enough to name Gavran in the same breath as Torin, even without the name
stakes.external: Torin's relationship with the technique is deepening; the wound's architecture is legible as a sustained human cost

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, then private corridor exchange
sensory_details: The Codex's records resolving into wound-mechanics — the anchor system as an engineered architecture, not a containment field; Torin's Force presence when he holds the Codex — the heaviness lifting into something lighter and more dangerous; Sera's jaw tight; Kael's expression saying without saying that both positions prove his point; Ben's understanding of the mechanism landing in his stomach a beat before it lands in his head
canon_elements_needed: Force wound theory with Nihilus and Malachor V precedent
Anchor system architecture — Force-sensitives used as structural load-bearing in a sealed wound
Jedi Lords era containment engineering; twelve-anchor configuration rationale
action_beats: Torin lifts the Codex fragment and holds it steady while the others watch for a reaction that doesn't come

The fragment's records resolve — the wound's mechanism named, the anchor system specified, twelve living Force-sensitives as sustained structural rebar. R04c lands. Ben registers the mechanism through his body before his mind processes it
Torin's reading of the same material lands as correction-not-violation — coherent, beautiful, dangerous
Sera steps close enough to place her hand flat on the table between Torin and the artifact
Sera pulls Ben into the corridor and speaks with her back to the common area door
notes: R04c is the Ch 9 deferred revelation per D8 — wound mechanics named, anchor system specified. This must land before Ch 13's midpoint so that Ben's breach experience at Kolven is informed by the understanding that the Scar's architecture is built from people. Do not pull R04d (Brotherhood inversion, Ch 11) into this scene. Torin's rationalisation has to be genuinely compelling on the page — the reader who finishes the scene thinking 'Torin is obviously wrong' is the reader the book has already lost. Sera's warning is a single line and a hand on an arm, not a monologue. Per R11, Ben's close-third does not narrate his 'near-seduction' as a self-analysis. The nod catches in his body, he stops it, Sera sees him catch it. The reader registers the danger through the beat, not through interiority labelling it. Per D4, the wound's mechanism lands through body-experience — Ben feels the scale of it in his stomach before his head processes — not through analytical narration. Per R12, Torin's warmth register is preserved even as his argument sharpens; the warmth is what makes the argument dangerous. Per D7, narrator does not over-signal Torin's direction past Ben's perception; the scene renders Torin as Ben reads him — a man Ben could follow if he let himself. Torin's lie_reinforced: each justification strengthens him further. Sera's lie_reinforced: her rigid certainty feels validated by Torin's drift; she is right about the danger and not yet flexible about the response. Per D3, the technique and the wound sit inside Weave terminology — Torin may use 'the stitching' in-character. Anti-pattern: Sera does not name Gavran aloud; the comparison lands in the unsaid. Primary anchor: Luceno (payload-through-reaction — the wound's mechanism landing on Ben via Torin's reading rather than exposition); supporting anchor: Zahn (clean frame for the Codex beat); Bujold (Ben's interior register of his own near-nod). One Stover-permitted interior beat allowed at the moment the wound-mechanism lands in Ben's body.
